source_text: Δοίη τοίνυν ἡμῖν ὁ σωτὴρ ἐντεῦθεν ἀρξαμένοις τοῦ λόγου τἀληθῆ καὶ τὰ πρέποντα καὶ τὰ σωτήρια συμβαλέσθαι τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς πρός τε τὴν ἐλπίδα πρῶτον αὐτὴν καὶ δεύτερον πρὸς τὴν τῆς ἐλπίδος προσαγωγήν. ὃ δὲ χαρίζεται δεομένοις καὶ αἰτοῦντας διδάσκει καὶ λύει τὴν ἄγνοιαν καὶ τὴν ἀπόγνωσιν ἀποσείεται, τοὺς αὐτοὺς πάλιν εἰσάγων λόγους περὶ τῶν πλουσίων. ἑαυτῶν ἑρμηνέας γινομένους καὶ ἐξηγητὰς ἀσφαλεῖς. οὐδὲν γὰρ οἷον αὐτῶν αὖθις ἀκοῦσαι τῶν ῥητῶν. ἅπερ ἡμᾶς ἐν τοῖς εὐαγγελίοις ἄχρι νῦν διετάρασσεν ἀβασανίστως καὶ διημαρτημένως ὑπὸ νηπιότητος ἀκροωμένους. »ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ εἰς ὁδὸν προσελθών τις ἐγονυπέτει λέγων· ›διδάσκαλε ἀγαθέ, τί ποιήσω, ἵνα ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω;‹ ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς λέγει· τί με ἀγαθὸν λέγεις; οὐδεὶς ἀγαθὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ θεός. τὰς ἐντολὰς οἶδας· μὴ μοιχεύσῃς, μὴ φονεύσῃς, μὴ κλέψῃς, μὴ ψευδομαρτυρήσῃς, τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα ὃ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς λέγει αὐτῷ· ›πάντα ταῦτα ἐφύλαξα ἐκ νεότητός μου. ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐμβλέψας ἠγάπησεν αὐτὸν καὶ εἶπεν· ›ἕν σοι ὑστερεῖ· εἰ θέλεις τέλειος εἶναι, πώλησον ὅσα ἔχεις καὶ διάδος πτωχοῖς, καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν οὐρανῷ, καὶ δεῦρο ἀκολούθει μοι.‹ ὃ δὲ στυγνάσας ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ ἀπῆλθε λυπούμενος· ἦν γὰρ ἔχων χρήματα πολλὰ καὶ ἀγρούς. περιβλεψάμενος δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· ›πῶς δυσκόλως οἱ τὰ χρήμα τα ἔχοντες εἰσελεύσονται εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.‹ οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἐθαμβοῦντο ἐπὶ τοῖς λόγοις αὐτοῦ. πάλιν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀποκριθεὶς λέγει αὐτοῖς· ›τέκνα, πῶς δύσκολόν ἐστι τοὺς πεποιθότας ἐπὶ χρήμασιν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν· εὐκόλως διὰ τῆς τρυμαλιᾶς τῆς βελόνης κάμηλος εἰσελεύσεται ἢ πλούσιος εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.‹ οἳ δὲ περισσῶς ἐξεπλήσσοντο καὶ ἔλεγον· ›τίς οὖν δύναται σωθῆναι;‹ ὃ δὲ ἐμβλέψας αὐτοῖς εἶπεν· ›ὅ τι παρὰ ἀνθρώποις ἀδύνατον, παρὰ θεῷ δυνατόν.‹ ἤρξατο ὁ Πέτρος λέγειν αὐτῷ· ›ἴδε ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν πάντα καὶ ἠκολουθήσαμέν σοι.‹ ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς [λέγγει]·› ἀμὴν ὑμῖν λέγω, ὃς ἂν ἀφῇ τὰ ἴδια καὶ γονεῖς καὶ ἀδελφοὺς καὶ χρήματα ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ καὶ ἕνεκεν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου. ἀπολήψεται ἑκατονταπλασίονα. νῦν ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τούτῳ ἀγροὺς καὶ χρήματα καὶ οἰκίας καὶ ἀδελφοὺς ἔχειν μετὰ διωγμὼν εἰς ποῦ: ἐν δὲ τῷ ἐρχομένῳ ζωή[ν] ἐστιν αἰώνιος.
thought_title: The Gospel dialogue on the rich man, retold as the true starting point
orientation: Clement has just described the Christian life as a contest; now he prays that the Savior will help him interpret the Gospel passage about the rich man, and he quotes the dialogue from Mark 10 at length.
pass_a_gloss: May the Savior grant to us, who have begun the discourse from this point, to contribute the true things and the fitting things and the saving things to the brothers, first toward the hope itself and second toward the approach to the hope. What he grants to those who ask, he also teaches those who ask, and he dissolves the ignorance and shakes off the despair, bringing in again the same words about rich persons, words that become interpreters of themselves and safe expounders. For there is nothing like hearing the sayings themselves again. These sayings disturbed us in the gospels until now, when we listened to them unexaminedly and mistakenly because of childishness. As he was going out into the road, someone came up and knelt before him, saying: Good teacher, what shall I do, in order that I may inherit eternal life? And Jesus says: Why do you call me good? No one is good except one, God. You know the commandments: do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honor your father and your mother. And he answered and says to him: All these I have kept from my youth. And Jesus looked at him and loved him and said: One thing is lacking to you; if you wish to be perfect, sell as much as you have and distribute to poor persons, and you will have treasure in heaven, and come, follow me. And he, becoming gloomy at the word, went away grieving; for he was having much money and fields. And Jesus looked around and says to his disciples: How difficultly those who have money will enter into the kingdom of God. And the disciples were astounded at his words. And again Jesus answered and says to them: Children, how difficult it is for those who have trusted in money to enter into the kingdom of God; more easily a camel will enter through the eye of the needle than a rich person into the kingdom of God. And they were exceedingly astonished and said: Who then can be saved? And he looked at them and said: What is impossible with human beings is possible with God. Peter began to say to him: See, we have left everything and have followed you. And Jesus answered [says]: Amen I say to you, whoever leaves his own things and parents and brothers and money for my sake and for the sake of the gospel will receive a hundredfold. Now in this time to have fields and money and houses and brothers with persecutions into where? But in the coming one there is eternal life.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'poor person' for πτωχός, and the dative plural here is the indirect object of 'distribute'; 'poor persons' preserves the glossary form in the plural.
The glossary requires 'rich person' for πλούσιος, and the nominative singular here is the subject of the comparison; 'rich person' preserves the glossary form.
The glossary requires 'money' for χρήματα, and the plural accusative here refers to material goods; 'money' preserves the glossary form.
The glossary requires 'eternal life' for ζωὴ αἰώνιος, and the accusative here is the object of 'inherit'; 'eternal life' preserves the glossary form.

The source text here says 'kingdom of God' (not 'kingdom of heaven'), so I render it literally as 'kingdom of God' to match the source wording, even though the glossary entry is for 'kingdom of heaven'.
The glossary requires 'treasure' for θησαυρός, and the phrase is a direct quotation from the Gospel; 'treasure in heaven' preserves the glossary form and the literal wording.

pass_b_english: May the Savior grant us, then, as we begin the discourse from this point, to contribute what is true, fitting, and saving to our brothers and sisters—first for hope itself, and second for the approach to hope. What He grants to those who ask, He also teaches to those who request it, and He dissolves ignorance and shakes off despair by bringing forward again the same words about rich persons, words that become their own interpreters and sure expounders. For there is nothing like hearing the sayings themselves again—the very sayings that until now have troubled us when we listened to them unexaminedly and mistakenly, out of childishness.

“As He was setting out on the road, a man ran up and knelt before Him, saying, ‘Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?’ Jesus said to him, ‘Why do you call me good? No one is good except one—God. You know the commandments: do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honor your father and your mother.’ He answered Him, ‘I have kept all these from my youth.’ Jesus looked at him, loved him, and said, ‘One thing you lack: if you wish to be perfect, sell what you have and distribute it to poor persons, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.’ But he became gloomy at the word and went away grieving, for he had much money and lands.” (Mark 10:17-22)

“Jesus looked around and said to His disciples, ‘How hard it will be for those who have money to enter the kingdom of God.’ The disciples were astounded at His words. But Jesus answered again and said to them, ‘Children, how hard it is for those who trust in money to enter the kingdom of God. It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.’ They were exceedingly astonished and said, ‘Then who can be saved?’ He looked at them and said, ‘What is impossible with human beings is possible with God.’” (Mark 10:23-27)

“Peter began to say to Him, ‘Look, we have left everything and followed you.’ Jesus answered, ‘Truly I tell you, whoever leaves his own things and parents and brothers and sisters and money for my sake and for the sake of the gospel will receive a hundredfold—now in this present time fields and money and houses and brothers and sisters, with persecutions—and in the age to come eternal life.’” (Mark 10:28-30)
notes: The source text has [λέγγει] in brackets, which appears to be a scribal error or variant for λέγει; I have rendered it as 'says' and noted the bracket.
The source text has ζωή[ν] with a bracketed nu, indicating a possible scribal correction or uncertainty; I have rendered it as 'life' in the accusative.
The source text has 'εἰς ποῦ:' which appears to be a truncated or damaged phrase; I have rendered it literally as 'into where?' and noted the uncertainty.
The source text has 'διωγμὼν' with an omega, which appears to be a variant spelling for διωγμῶν; I have rendered it as 'persecutions'.

problems.quote: He dissolves ignorance and shakes off despair
problems.why: Greek mentions only ignorance, not despair; “despair” adds a concept not in the source.
problems.ruling: Source has λύει τὴν ἄγνοιαν καὶ τὴν ἀπόγνωσιν; translator omitted ἀπόγνωσιν ('despair') after 'dissolves', breaking the sentence.

edits.old: He dissolves ignorance and shakes off despair

fixed: Removed "and shakes off despair" because the source has only "λύει τὴν ἄγνοιαν" (dissolves the ignorance); "despair" is not in the Greek.

problems.source_quote: λύει τὴν ἄγνοιαν καὶ τὴν ἀπόγνωσιν ἀποσείεται
problems.why: Source says He dissolves ignorance AND shakes off despair; English drops the second clause.
problems.fix: and He dissolves ignorance and shakes off despair
problems.ruling: Source: λύει τὴν ἄγνοιαν καὶ τὴν ἀπόγνωσιν ἀποσείεται; English only 'He dissolves ignorance', omits 'and casts away despair'.

edits.old: and He dissolves ignorance by bringing forward again
edits.new: and He dissolves ignorance and shakes off despair by bringing forward again

fixed: Omission confirmed: source λύει τὴν ἄγνοιαν καὶ τὴν ἀπόγνωσιν ἀποσείεται has two coordinated verbs (dissolves ignorance AND shakes off despair); English dropped the second clause. Restored with minimal insertion.

last_rejected.quote: and you will have treasure in heaven
last_rejected.ruling: English includes “and you will have treasure in heaven” matching source καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν οὐρανῷ

last_rejected.source_quote: λύει τὴν ἄγνοιαν καὶ τὴν ἀπόγνωσιν ἀποσείεται
last_rejected.why: Greek mentions ignorance and lack of knowledge, not despair; English adds a concept not in the source.
last_rejected.fix: dissolves ignorance and lack of knowledge
last_rejected.ruling: ἀπόγνωσις means despair/hopelessness, not 'lack of knowledge'; ἄγνοια is ignorance. 'Shakes off despair' correctly renders ἀποσείεται τὴν ἀπόγνωσιν.
